currentContext.business: Subex sells AI-led software and services to Communications Service Providers (CSPs) and other telecom operators, spanning Business Assurance, Fraud Management, Partner Ecosystem Management, Managed Services and Business Consulting. The Company combines deep telecom domain expertise with artificial intelligence and advanced analytics so operators can protect revenues, manage operational complexity and strengthen digital confidence across interconnected telecom ecosystems. currentContext.expansion: The routed sections disclose no plant, capacity, capex project, delivery-centre addition, acquisition or JV. Subex is an asset-light telecom software company and its expansion narrative is product- and market-led rather than capacity-led: the Company describes building out its portfolio of Fraud Management, Business Assurance, Partner Ecosystem Management, Managed Services and Business Consulting Services around the HyperSense, ROC, FraudZap and AI Agent Squad platforms, and during FY26 continued to embed AI and advanced analytics across the Business Assurance portfolio to move customers from reactive assurance to predictive, outcome-driven assurance. On market footprint, management states the addressable market for what Subex does was $0.19 billion three years ago and is $4.3 billion today, with expansion opportunities in telecom adjacencies such as mobile money, fintech, IoT, MVNO/MVNE services and digital infrastructure. No commissioning dates, capacity figures or capital-expenditure plans of the Company itself are disclosed in this text; the only capital-expenditure discussion relates to customers' (CSPs') network spending, which management flags as a demand risk when constrained.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange risk from export concentration
risks.note: A significant portion of revenue is derived from international markets - exports contributed 99% of total turnover - exposing the Company to currency fluctuations, particularly USD/INR, which may impact profitability and cash flows; mitigated through a calibrated hedging strategy that maintains prudent hedge coverage on net foreign currency exposure while retaining flexibility to benefit from favourable moves.

risks.risk: Talent and capability risk in an AI-scarce labour market
risks.note: Rapid adoption of AI and digital technologies has intensified competition for specialised talent, and the ability to attract, develop and retain skilled professionals is critical to sustaining innovation and execution; permanent-employee turnover was 22% in FY26 (24% FY25, 33% FY24). Mitigation includes building an AI-native workforce through targeted capability development, GenAI-enabled engineering practices, Code Shield workshops and adoption of GitHub Copilot.

Increasing cyber threats, evolving data privacy regulations and rising expectations on responsible AI usage elevate compliance and security requirements; failure to address them could impact customer trust, reputation and business performance. BRSR identifies Data Privacy and Security as a material risk, given regulatory penalties, legal liabilities, operational disruption and reputational damage from non-compliance or cyber incidents.

risks.risk: Technology disruption and competitive intensity / market positioning
risks.note: Rapid advances in AI platforms and managed agent ecosystems may alter customer preferences, while established global players, niche providers, hyperscalers and emerging AI-native companies compete for the same customers; intensifying competition may affect new-customer acquisition, retention, pricing and market share. Mitigation is continuous benchmarking plus a balanced mix of proprietary innovation and selected third-party AI capabilities.

Growing demand for GenAI solutions increases dependence on specialised computing infrastructure including GPUs; supply constraints and extended procurement lead times may affect product development and customer deployments. Mitigated by optimising solution architectures, using a mix of on-premise and cloud infrastructure, and deploying open-source AI models for selected use cases.

risks.risk: Project execution and supply chain dependency on customer readiness
risks.note: Delays in customer-side infrastructure readiness and extended hardware procurement cycles may affect implementation timelines; addressed via cloud-based deployment alternatives, embedding infrastructure-readiness requirements in project planning, and working with approved vendor ecosystems.

risks.risk: Customer capital-expenditure discipline and demand deferral
risks.note: The telecom industry operates under disciplined capital allocation; during periods of constrained capex, CSPs may defer or reprioritise investments in digital transformation, operational modernisation and business support platforms, directly affecting demand for Subex's software and business assurance platforms. CSPs are expected to remain selective, prioritising spend that delivers measurable improvements.

Geopolitical tensions, regional conflicts, trade restrictions and evolving regulatory landscapes may delay customer investment decisions, disrupt project execution and create demand volatility across geographies; restrictions on cross-border operations and supply chains may hinder implementation and technology deployment.

one-line thesis: Subex has completed its operational reset with 3 consecutive quarters of positive PAT and a 24% YoY order intake growth, signaling a shift from defense to offense. While FY26 revenue grew only 6% due to base effects from non-core exits, the strong backlog and successful AI product commercialization (FraudZap) position FY27 for accelerated conversion, though Middle East geopolitical risks remain a monitored variable.

guidance: Revenue Growth: Bullish on FY27 expecting to beat FY26 benchmarks driven by backlog conversion; Margin: Targeting EBITDA expansion via AI-led R&D efficiency; Order Inflow: Momentum continuing despite some Middle East contracting delays; Capex: Focused on GPU/Hardware optimization for AI models.

growth verticals / optionality: FraudZap AI solution now has 3 paying telco customers via intermediary; 'Team of LLMs' product completed POCs, awaiting commercial signing (delayed by customer GPU hardware constraints); Expansion into Americas and Africa to offset Middle East volatility.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA improvement driven by strict cost optimization in R&D (benchmarking 12-15% of cost) and GTM; GenAI adoption in development reducing engineering costs; Operating expenses (R&D, Sales, G&A) sit below gross margin.

risks & watch-items: Geopolitical instability in Middle East (31% revenue exposure) causing contracting delays; Customer concentration (Top 10 = 60%); Hardware availability (GPUs) for AI product deployment; Lack of promoter holding (diverse retail base).
management quality / tone: Confident and assertive on turnaround completion; Acknowledges stock undervaluation; Transparent about Middle East risks but emphasizes mitigation via offshoring; Bullish on FY27 conversion.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly states the market has not caught up with fundamentals; AI is viewed as a 'tailwind' enhancing their System of Record rather than a disruptor; Goodwill of INR 190 Cr+ passed impairment test despite past concerns.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.

hero.oneLiner: Subex Limited is a telecom AI solutions provider with over three decades of industry expertise, helping communications service providers mitigate risk, combat fraud, assure revenue and optimise partner ecosystems.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Subex Limited is a telecom AI solutions provider with over three decades of industry expertise, helping communications service providers mitigate risk, combat fraud, assure revenue and optimise partner ecosystems.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Subex sells AI-led software and services to Communications Service Providers (CSPs) and other telecom operators, spanning Business Assurance, Fraud Management, Partner Ecosystem Management, Managed Services and Business Consulting. The Company combines deep telecom domain expertise with artificial intelligence and advanced analytics so operators can protect revenues, manage operational complexity and strengthen digital confidence across interconnected telecom ecosystems. Revenue is earned through support and other services, license/implementation & customisation, and managed services, with almost all of it coming from customers outside India.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global telecom industry is shifting from connectivity to intelligence, with operators monetising digital infrastructure through AI, cloud, advanced analytics and data centres as 5G investments mature
- Global Telecom Outlook projects global telecommunications revenues to reach approximately US$1.32 trillion by 2029, a CAGR of 2.8%
- Subex's addressable market expanded from approximately US$0.19 billion to approximately US$4.3 billion over three years
- Telecom industry loses US$42 billion annually to fraud, equal to 2.46% of revenues, and that loss is growing at nearly six times the rate of industry revenue itself
- Device fraud was the single largest fraud type in 2025, accounting for 10% of all global fraud losses
- CSPs are diversifying into IoT, enterprise connectivity, private 5G, cloud services, fintech and mobile money, content platforms and API-driven services, creating far greater operational complexity across networks, billing, partner management and revenue assurance
- Operators are shifting from rule-based fraud systems to intelligent, continuously learning platforms capable of real-time detection and prevention
- Agentic AI is enabling operators to automate investigation, assurance, partner management and operational workflows
- Rise of AI-generated identities, voice cloning and deepfake-enabled fraud is increasing demand for advanced authentication and identity verification
- Growing emphasis on digital sovereignty, data privacy, cybersecurity resilience and responsible AI governance is reshaping enterprise technology priorities
- Enterprise spending on strategic technology initiatives remained resilient despite inflationary pressures, geopolitical developments, trade dynamics and regulatory change
- Telecom operators are expected to maintain investments in initiatives that enhance operational efficiency, strengthen digital trust, enable service innovation and support business transformation
- Constrained telecom capital expenditure could cause CSPs to defer or reprioritise digital transformation and business support platform investments, affecting demand
- Revenue mix commentary: Support & others continues to be the largest revenue contributor, followed by License, Implementation & customisation and Managed services
- India is strengthening its position as a global innovation hub for next-generation telecom and digital technologies, supported by digital public infrastructure, deep technology talent and nationwide 5G rollout
- More than 80% of new business wins in FY26 incorporated AI use cases
- Near-complete renewal success across strategic customer accounts; 92% of customers renewed with value retention of 98%
- FraudZap was built and contracted within six months of inception
- Early-stage contracts are to be converted into recurring revenue at scale as an FY27 priority

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA improvement driven by strict cost optimization in R&D (benchmarking 12-15% of cost) and GTM; GenAI adoption in development reducing engineering costs; Operating expenses (R&D, Sales, G&A) sit below gross margin.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Liquidity increased by INR 70 Cr in FY26; No dividends mentioned; Focus on reinvestment for growth and potential M&A integration readiness; Management increasing skin-in-game via ESOPs.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections disclose no plant, capacity, capex project, delivery-centre addition, acquisition or JV. Subex is an asset-light telecom software company and its expansion narrative is product- and market-led rather than capacity-led: the Company describes building out its portfolio of Fraud Management, Business Assurance, Partner Ecosystem Management, Managed Services and Business Consulting Services around the HyperSense, ROC, FraudZap and AI Agent Squad platforms, and during FY26 continued to embed AI and advanced analytics across the Business Assurance portfolio to move customers from reactive assurance to predictive, outcome-driven assurance. On market footprint, management states the addressable market for what Subex does was $0.19 billion three years ago and is $4.3 billion today, with expansion opportunities in telecom adjacencies such as mobile money, fintech, IoT, MVNO/MVNE services and digital infrastructure. No commissioning dates, capacity figures or capital-expenditure plans of the Company itself are disclosed in this text; the only capital-expenditure discussion relates to customers' (CSPs') network spending, which management flags as a demand risk when constrained.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and assertive on turnaround completion; Acknowledges stock undervaluation; Transparent about Middle East risks but emphasizes mitigation via offshoring; Bullish on FY27 conversion.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over three decades of telecom domain expertise underpinning its solution portfolio
- AI, GenAI and advanced-analytics capability embedded across Business Assurance, Fraud Management and Partner Ecosystem Management
- Long-standing relationships with several of the world's leading telecommunications companies
- Recognised for the second consecutive year in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI in CSP Customer and Business Operations
- Broad, integrated portfolio spanning assurance, fraud, partner management, managed services and consulting that addresses an estimated US$4.3 billion addressable market
- Lightweight, plug-and-play deployment model (FraudZap) enabling faster implementation and time-to-value versus traditional fraud management deployments

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical instability in Middle East (31% revenue exposure) causing contracting delays; Customer concentration (Top 10 = 60%); Hardware availability (GPUs) for AI product deployment; Lack of promoter holding (diverse retail base).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly states the market has not caught up with fundamentals; AI is viewed as a 'tailwind' enhancing their System of Record rather than a disruptor; Goodwill of INR 190 Cr+ passed impairment test despite past concerns.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Enter FY27 driving three priorities: grow the core telco business faster, expand the AI product portfolio in fraud management and agentic operations, and convert early-stage contracts into recurring revenue at scale
- Reposition Subex from a legacy RAFM vendor into the intelligence layer for the telecom industry, articulated through the 'New Possibilities Now Possible' brand identity unveiled at the Global User Conference in Athens in November 2025
- Establish category leadership in Telecom AI within the three-to-five-year window management believes is open
- Build fast and deploy early against …
